deviation: The cap is 0.25x trailing-12-month fees, far below the 1x standard and 2x fallback, so Arcadia's recoverable losses would be minimal. The draft also has no carve-outs from the cap or the exclusions for IP infringement indemnity or breach of confidentiality (11.4 covers only fraud and non-excludable liability). Section 11.2 excludes data loss, regulatory fines, notification costs and substitute procurement costs, and 11.3 removes supplier liability for events outside its control and for customer backups, which leaves Arcadia with little recourse for data breaches.
suggested_text:
11.1 Subject to Section 11.4, each party's total aggregate liability arising under or in connection with this Agreement, whether in contract, tort (including negligence), breach of statutory duty or otherwise, shall not exceed 1 times the annual fees paid or payable under this Agreement.

11.2 Subject to Section 11.4, neither party shall be liable for indirect or consequential loss. For clarity, the following are recoverable direct losses and are not excluded: costs of procuring substitute services, regulatory fines and data breach notification and remediation costs, and costs of restoring lost or corrupted data, to the extent caused by the Supplier's breach.

11.3 [Delete. Supplier's exclusions for customer-caused matters should be addressed through a narrowly drafted, fault-based mitigation provision. They must not exclude liability for the Supplier's own breach of its security, data protection or business continuity obligations.]

11.4 Nothing in this Agreement limits or excludes either party's liability for: (a) fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation; (b) death or personal injury caused by negligence; (c) the IP infringement indemnity; (d) breach of confidentiality; or (e) any liability that cannot be limited or excluded under applicable law. The Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees is not subject to the cap in Section 11.1.

11.5 [Delete.]

Fallback, if required: in Section 11.1, replace "1 times" with "2 times". The 11.4 carve-outs remain mandatory.
